title: Short Stuff: The Science of Funny Words
summary: Short Stuff episode on the science of funny words. Josh and Chuck discuss University of Alberta psychologist Chris Westbury's study, "Wrigglely Squiffy lummocks and boobs colon what makes some words funny?", which started from a list of 5,000 English words rated funniest by people and built a mathematical model to rank words by funniness. The top ten funniest words include "wriggly," "giggle," "guffaw," "puffball," and "jiggly"; runners-up include "squiffy," "flappy," "bucko," "poop," "puke," and "boobs." Westbury used a co-occurrence tool to group words into six categories (expletives, sex, the body, partying, animals, insults). The funniest words relate roughly equally to several categories. Form matters too: rarer letter sounds (such as K) make words funnier, tying into incongruity theory of humor. The episode closes with a quote from The Sunshine Boys about funny words (Alka Seltzer, Casey Stengel, cupcake, pickle, chicken).

entities.name: Wriggly Squiffy Lummocks and Boobs: What Makes Some Words Funny?

segments.title: Opening banter and funny words
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with funny-sounding words like poop and buddy wiggle, introduce Chris Westbury and his study on why some words are funny, and mention the list of funny-sounding place names.

segments.title: Top ten funniest words and farting
segments.summary: The hosts describe Westbury's method of starting with 5,000 English words rated funniest in a poll and building a model to rank every word. They list the top ten funniest words and runners-up, and joke about poop, puke, boobs, and farting.

segments.title: Incongruity theory of humor
segments.summary: Josh explains incongruity theory, the idea that unexpected outcomes are funny, and says Westbury wanted to quantify it rather than accept it as common sense.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Brief break with banter about Westbury and the hosts' jokes before the explanation of the method continues.

segments.title: Six semantic categories and co-occurrence
segments.summary: Westbury ran a sample of several hundred of the funniest words through a co-occurrence tool and found they fall into six categories: expletives, sex, the body, partying, animals, and insults. Words that relate roughly equally to several categories, like poop, tend to be funnier.

segments.title: Word form, letter sounds, and rarity
segments.summary: Westbury also looked at word form, including length and individual sounds. Rarer sounds such as K make words funnier, as in pickle versus tomato. Unexpected, improbable words trigger the incongruity response, as with Walla Walla Washington.

segments.title: The Sunshine Boys quote and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close with a quote from The Sunshine Boys in which Walter Matthau's character lists funny words such as Alka Seltzer, Casey Stengel, cupcake, and pickle, and then sign off.
